purpose: Does a Thai lexical (BM25) side help dense parent-child retrieval, which tokenizer/dictionary, which BM25 parameters, which fusion? Every candidate value below carries the source it came from; nothing is guessed.
selection_rule: Declared before running. Stage by stage, keep the setting with the highest hybrid Recall@5 on dev (ties: higher MRR@10). Report the paired bootstrap difference against the stage's reference. If the 95% interval of that difference includes 0 the result is labelled 'not distinguishable': the setting is carried forward only as provisional, and the literature default stays the reference. The questions are silver (AI drafts); every number must be re-checked on gold before it is used.

bm25_params.source: bm25s 0.3.12 library defaults (BM25.__init__ signature), Lucene scoring variant

fusion.source: Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher, SIGIR 2009: k = 60 fixed in a pilot and never changed

variants.name: newmm
variants.why: default PyThaiNLP dictionary; the baseline whose failures (HbA1c -> HbA|1|c) motivated the test

variants.name: newmm_latin
variants.why: keeps Latin/digit runs whole (HbA1c, eGFR, mg/dL); rule-based, no dictionary

variants.name: newmm_dict_df5
variants.why: 28 corpus-learned words (fragments outside the default dictionary that occur almost only inside one run; scripts/learn_thai_dictionary.py)

variants.name: char3
variants.why: no dictionary at all: character trigrams. Indirect support only: character n-grams avoid the dictionary problem and are reported to work well for languages without word boundaries (SIGIR 2008 poster on unsupervised segmentation; a Thai n-gram indexing paper). No paper compares them on Thai retrieval directly.

variants.name: char4
variants.why: character 4-grams, same reasoning as char3 (longer grams are more specific)

settings.name: anserini_default
settings.source: Anserini/Pyserini defaults (Lin et al., Pyserini, arXiv 2102.10073)

settings.name: anserini_msmarco_tuned
settings.source: Anserini MS MARCO passage tuned values (Pyserini docs / arXiv 2102.10073)

settings.name: anserini_tuned_for_expansion
settings.source: Anserini 'tuned2', tuned on doc2query-T5 expanded passages (Pyserini, arXiv 2102.10073); relevant because doc2query is tested later

settings.name: rz_range_low
settings.source: corner of the range 1.2<k1<2, 0.5<b<0.8 attributed to Robertson & Zaragoza 2009 (cited second-hand in arXiv 1608.01573)

settings.name: rz_range_high
settings.source: other corner of the same range

stage_b_bm25_params.note: Kamphuis et al. (ECIR 2020, 'Which BM25 do you mean?') found no significant differences between BM25 scoring variants on newswire, so the Lucene variant is used throughout and only k1/b are varied.

rrf_k.source: 60 is Cormack et al. 2009. The other values are ours, chosen to bracket 60 on both sides because Bruch, Gai & Ingber 2023 (arXiv 2210.11934) report that RRF is sensitive to its parameter.

convex_alpha.source: Bruch et al. 2023: convex combination of normalised scores has one parameter, is sample-efficient to tune and was reported to beat RRF; normalisation choice mattered little. The 0.1 grid is ours.
